assessment.nobel_worthiness: Pd-catalyzed C-N cross-coupling made aryl amines, ubiquitous in drugs, materials and natural-product intermediates, accessible with broad scope and predictable ligand design. It is a general, step-economical method that reshaped retrosynthesis and is used daily at industrial scale; originality is high and the impact is lasting.
assessment.attribution: Buchwald and Hartwig independently developed the catalytic, ligand-controlled version in the mid-1990s and then the modern ligand generations; Kosugi's earlier tin-amide work is a precursor, and Migita is not credited here. A Buchwald-Hartwig pair is the natural, fair configuration, though the precursor credit is debatable.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed across thousands of applications in academia and industry for 25+ years; the interpretation is stable and recognition is, if anything, overdue.
uncertainties: Whether the Kosugi/Migita precursor work requires acknowledgment in the citation.
Overlap with the 2010 Pd cross-coupling prize may lead some members to see it as incremental, though the C-N bond-forming chemistry is distinct.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Visible-light photoredox catalysis opened new radical and single-electron pathways with mild conditions and now supports a wide range of bond constructions, including in total synthesis and late-stage functionalization. It is a clear conceptual shift in how reactive intermediates are generated.
assessment.attribution: Yoon, Stephenson and Nicewicz independently introduced the key synthetic reactions around 2008-2011, with MacMillan's concurrent work already recognised in the 2021 organocatalysis prize, which complicates credit. The list also includes König, Melchiorre and Fukuzumi, all with real claims, so any three leave out strong contributors.
assessment.maturity: Broadly reproduced and heavily adopted, including in pharma; the field is still evolving but the core principle is firmly established.
uncertainties: Partial overlap with the 2021 Nobel Prize and MacMillan's role.
Credit is spread among many groups, so a three-person selection is unavoidably contested.
Earlier photochemistry (Fukuzumi, Kellogg, Cano-Yelo and Deronzier) may predate the synthetic breakthrough.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Catalytic C-H functionalization turns ubiquitous C-H bonds into synthetic handles, changing step economy and disconnection logic in synthesis. Directing-group, ligand-controlled and template strategies deliver site selectivity that was previously impossible.
assessment.attribution: Yu's ligand-enabled Pd(II) catalysis and remote-selectivity templates, Sanford's Pd(II)/(IV) and mechanistic work, and Hartwig's Ir borylation form a coherent, diverse set. Bergman's alkane activation (B019) and Murai's work are earlier foundations and could merit separate recognition.
assessment.maturity: Widely adopted in methodology, medicinal chemistry and total synthesis; maturity is good, although industrial scope for the most selective systems is still developing.
uncertainties: The field is diffuse, so the citation might be too broad or a scientifically arbitrary subset.
Hartwig appears in two candidates, which affects how the committee should weigh the two.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Targeted protein degradation reframes small-molecule pharmacology as induced proximity: bifunctional PROTACs and molecular glues make the ubiquitin-proteasome system programmable. The impact is rapid, with several degraders in clinical trials, and the molecular understanding of cereblon and VHL is chemically rich.
assessment.attribution: Crews (PROTAC concept and first realisation with Deshaies) and Handa (cereblon as the thalidomide target) are decisive; Ciulli contributed VHL ligand and structural design of degraders. Deshaies is excluded from my triple despite his early co-authorship, which is a real attribution tension.
assessment.maturity: Strong mechanistic confirmation, but clinical validation is still incomplete, so recognition could be premature for this ranking.
uncertainties: Absence of an approved PROTAC drug.
Complicated attribution between PROTAC concept holders and the thalidomide-target discovery.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Solexa sequencing-by-synthesis, based on reversible terminator nucleotide chemistry and clonal surface amplification, transformed genomics and biomedicine. The core is rational design of nucleotide and linker chemistry, which is a chemical invention with enormous impact.
assessment.attribution: Balasubramanian and Klenerman conceived and developed the method; Rothberg's pyrosequencing platform is a separate technology, and Mayer's and Ju's work are related but less decisive for the dominant platform. A two-person prize looks fair, but the clean credit is disputed in this crowded field.
assessment.maturity: Fully mature with two decades of use across the biosciences; recognition is well timed.
uncertainties: Whether the committee views this as chemistry or as biological technology.
Competing platform claims (454, Ju's work) complicate the citation.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Base editing introduced a deaminase-chemistry-based way to rewrite single nucleotides without double-strand breaks, combining protein engineering and directed evolution. It is conceptually original and spurred clinical gene-editing programmes.
assessment.attribution: Liu led the conceptual and engineering effort; Komor and Gaudelli were lead trainees on the cytosine and adenine base editors, and Nishida and Kondo reported an independent cytidine deaminase fusion. A prize with Liu alone is plausible, but the other credits are contested.
assessment.maturity: Clinical translation is just beginning and independent confirmation is strong, but long-term safety and durability are unsettled; I regard it as promising and slightly early.
uncertainties: Timing relative to the CRISPR prize and overlap with it.
Whether it is chemistry or molecular biology.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Native chemical ligation and expressed-protein ligation allow chemoselective assembly of large peptides and proteins, enabling total chemical protein synthesis and the study of post-translationally modified proteins. It is a clear, general reaction concept.
assessment.attribution: Kent and Dawson introduced native chemical ligation in 1994, and Muir's expressed-protein ligation extended it to semisynthesis. Danishefsky's refinements and Brik's and Liu's later contributions complicate credit, though a Kent-Dawson-Muir trio is well supported.
assessment.maturity: Well confirmed and used widely for 30 years; the field's impact is established, so recognition is on time or late.
uncertainties: Whether the committee sees later advances (Liu, Brik) as needing recognition.
The share between ligation chemistry and protein semisynthesis.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Isolation of stable carbenes (imidazolylidene, and cyclic alkyl amino carbenes) created a fundamentally new ligand and organocatalyst class, underlying Grubbs-type catalysts, main-group stabilisation, and organocatalytic umpolung. Originality is high, and the chemistry is clean and well understood.
assessment.attribution: Arduengo isolated the first crystalline N-heterocyclic carbene in 1991, and Bertrand's earlier phosphinocarbene (1988) and later CAAC work are distinct. Nolan, Rovis and Bode applied the carbenes in catalysis, so the decisive discoverers are Arduengo and Bertrand.
assessment.maturity: Mature, with decades of verified use; ripe for recognition but the field is broad, and part of the impact overlaps with the 2005 metathesis prize.
uncertainties: Whether recognition should favour discovery (Arduengo, Bertrand) or application in catalysis.
Overlap with the metathesis prize impact.
